rationale: Compiled artifacts faithfully realize the design: the seed_edits insert exactly the five message_reactions rows described in the roles (two matches for admins Robert Walsh and Morgan Freeman on the target message 1700173200.000456, and three negatives distinguishing wrong-role, wrong-message, and wholly-unrelated cases). The selector correctly instantiates the full assigned route REACTION→USER→WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP→WORKSPACE by joining message_reactions→users→user_teams→teams with filters role=admin and team_id=T01WORKSPACE, matching the route_nodes exactly (the compiler notes explicitly fixed this to avoid truncating at user_teams). All referenced users, their user_teams admin/member roles, and the target message were already present in the base seed and match the role facts stated in the design. The answer_attributes and Identifying paths are legitimate table.column names, and the near-miss set in mechanical_checks matches the intended negatives without introducing new accidental matches (computed_matches and computed_focal_negatives align with expected_matches/near_misses). The access_plan is realistic under the documented API (conversations.history/search for message location, reactions.get for reactions, users.info for the single workspace-role lookup per user, consistent with the runtime_qualifications about one workspace association per queried user). The task is legitimate bare retrieval with well-differentiated negatives (role-based, message-based, and unrelated), which is valid though not maximally consequential, keeping quality at adequate rather than strong.
